title: Religion and church music
summary: He was born Catholic, turned Methodist to remarry, and compares Baptist, Methodist and Catholic music and its rhythm and blues feel.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I was wondering, any church music did you hear? I'm not trying to pry into your affairs. I'm wondering what religion, you were a Methodist, I'm going to get it on to your... Yes. Were you always raised in a Methodist church?

No, I was born and raised Catholic. Oh really? I had my first wife Catholic. We divorced, those Catholics don't divorce you, you know. Yes, that's right. And when I met this wife, well she was Methodist and it's the only way that I could get married again, that by a Methodist preacher, you know, I figured if he was good enough to marry me, he was good enough for me to serve, to attend a subordinary in this church. So I turned Methodist.
There wasn't so much music, I guess, in the Catholic church, it was different there from any other city. No, no. Or worse, just as usual.
It was just a place that naturally caused me to change.
Yes, I mean I wondered the kind of music in the churches when you were young, if you heard anything like the Baptist and Methodist, the spiritual and God's hymn.

Well, I heard most of them because I was a young man, around 18, 20 years old. I used to visit all churches from time to time. I'd go to a Baptist church, I'd go to a Methodist church. I'd go to a Catholic church in the morning, Mass. See, my evenings were always free to go to a church. Sometimes I'd go to, I had some friends of mine who were Baptists, and I had some friends who were Methodists, I'd attend church with them. And I'd tell you from a musical standpoint, well, I prefer the Methodist music and the Catholics.

Well, people like Bud Scott and Mutt Carey, I know, told me years ago, and other people too, they even thought some of the early dance music, the jazz bands, were influenced by the music they heard in the churches.
Well, the Baptist has the same rhythm, and the style of singing is on the blue side.
It is. Most Baptists have their singing on the blue side. And they have the perfect rhythm.
You could dance to it as well as shout to it, you know what I mean?
They really enjoy themselves. Oh, yeah, they do. They do. They'll be happy in church. Well, that's right.
